title: Sinus tachycardia
summary: The sinus node fires faster than 100 per minute. Everything else about the beat is normal.

events.label: Sinus node
events.caption: The sinus node fires fast, here every 0.46 seconds, about 130 times a minute.

events.label: Normal conduction
events.caption: Each impulse follows the usual route to the ventricles, so the QRS is narrow.
events.ecg: A normal PR interval and a narrow QRS after every P wave.

events.label: Fast rate
events.caption: The rate is the only abnormality. It is usually a response to something, such as exercise, fever or illness.
events.ecg: Complexes close together, T waves running into the next P wave.

teaching_points: Sinus tachycardia is sinus rhythm at more than 100 per minute (slide 57).
It almost always has an underlying cause: treat the cause, not the rate.
